database_summary: Marketplace dataset (orders, customers, sellers, products, items, payments, reviews, geolocation and category translations). Core event grain is orders and order_items with supporting descriptive dimensions for customers, sellers, products and geolocation. Mix of current-state (customers, sellers, products), event/transaction rows (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews) and high-cardinality geolocation history/measurements.

accepted.name: orders_enriched_with_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
accepted.description: One row per order enriched with customer attributes. Use this when you need order-level facts along with customer location and customer_unique_id for grouping or joins to other order-level data. | Use for: order counts or revenue by customer attributes (city/state/unique customer); delivery lead time or delays per customer segment; linking reviews or payments back to customer demographics

accepted.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state
FROM olist_order_items oi
LEFT JOIN olist_products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN olist_sellers s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
grain: order_id, order_item_id (one row per order line item)
accepted.description: One row per order line item with product and seller descriptive attributes. Use for item-level revenue/freight analysis, product-level aggregation, or seller performance metrics. | Use for: item-level revenue, freight and price distributions; top products or sellers by revenue or count; analysis of product physical dimensions vs freight/costs

accepted.name: order_payments_agg_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value,
  COUNT(payment_sequential) AS payment_instruments_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(payment_sequential) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE AVG(payment_installments) END AS avg_payment_installments
FROM olist_order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: One row per order with aggregated payment metrics: total payment value, number of payment instruments, and average installment count. Use when you need order-level payment summaries (total paid, split payments). | Use for: total revenue per order; frequency of split payments; relationship between payment installments and order value

accepted.name: orders_with_payments_and_items_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  COALESCE(pagg.total_payment_value, 0) AS total_payment_value,
  COALESCE(pagg.payment_instruments_count, 0) AS payment_instruments_count,
  COALESCE(iagg.items_count, 0) AS items_count,
  COALESCE(iagg.items_total_price, 0) AS items_total_price,
  COALESCE(iagg.items_total_freight, 0) AS items_total_freight
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN order_payments_agg_by_order pagg
  ON o.order_id = pagg.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS items_count,
    SUM(price) AS items_total_price,
    SUM(freight_value) AS items_total_freight
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) iagg
  ON o.order_id = iagg.order_id
accepted.description: Order-level denormalized relation combining order attributes, customer info, payment aggregates and item-level aggregates (items count and total items revenue). Useful as a wide starting table for order lifecycle and revenue analyses. | Use for: order-level revenue and fulfillment performance; comparing paid amount vs items price/freight; cohorting orders by customer location or status

accepted.name: product_category_translation_lookup
accepted.description: One row per product_category_name with English translation. Use to normalize Portuguese category names to English for reporting and grouping. | Use for: translate product categories for dashboards; join product categories to English labels for exports

accepted.name: geolocation_zip_centroids
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  COUNT(*) AS geolocation_observations
FROM olist_geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Representative geolocation per zip code prefix: average latitude/longitude and count of observations. Useful to join zip-prefix-based customer or seller locations to a single lat/lng for mapping or distance calculations. | Use for: map customers or sellers by zip-code centroids; compute approximate distances between buyer and seller zip prefixes

accepted.name: orders_with_review_score
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  r.review_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_order_reviews r
  ON o.order_id = r.order_id
grain: order_id, review_id (one row per review; orders without reviews will appear with NULL review_* fields)
accepted.description: One row per order with its review score and review timestamps (if any). Useful to relate order delivery/purchase behavior to customer feedback. | Use for: average review_score by delivery delay or product category; identify orders with negative feedback; time between delivery and review creation

accepted.name: customers_repeat_purchase_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
  MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_purchase_timestamp,
  MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase_timestamp,
  SUM(COALESCE(pagg.total_payment_value, 0)) AS total_paid
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN order_payments_agg_by_order pagg
  ON o.order_id = pagg.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id, c.customer_unique_id
accepted.description: Customer-level purchase metrics: number of distinct orders, total spend (from payments), and first/last purchase timestamps. Use for customer lifetime and retention analyses. | Use for: identify repeat vs one-time customers; compute customer lifetime value approximations; cohort analysis by first_purchase_timestamp

accepted.name: latest_review_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  review_id,
  order_id,
  review_score,
  review_comment_title,
  review_comment_message,
  review_creation_date,
  review_answer_timestamp
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY review_creation_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM olist_order_reviews r
) sub
WHERE rn = 1
grain: order_id (one row per order with the latest review)
accepted.description: For orders with multiple reviews (if present), pick the latest review per order by review_creation_date. Use when you need one review row per order for analysis. | Use for: join single review to orders for sentiment analysis; compute average review score per product or seller using latest review
